name: @dsh-agent/dsh-agent-memory
description: Agent-facing memory layer (increment 1, I1 foundation + I1.2 scoring calibration + I2 residual-pyramid triage): four narrow tools (remember/recall/expand/prune) over a human-readable NDJSON store with a fail-closed write protocol, atomic writes, hard caps with score-based eviction, and zero runtime dependencies. I1.2 scoring: BM25 with per-field statistics, absolute-scale display (no batch normalization), VCP-style tag coverage as a diagnostic column, and MMR diversity multiplied into the printed score. I2 triage: a Gram-Schmidt residual pyramid over the tag-idf lexical space (novelty = 0.7*residualRatio + 0.3*directionConsistency) decides whether recall widens kBase -> kExpanded; all pyramid state is request-local (no module-level cache), and low confidence is only reported, never used to veto. I4a: two query-independent injection contributions sharing a single injection.enabled switch — a trailing runtime-context block (ctx.systemPrompt.context({name:'agent-memory', order:200, text})) carrying the library index (count + what the store is + a conditional rule + qualified tag anchors, changing only when the store changes, hard maxChars budget with an honest omission marker) and, since I4a.3, a stable section (ctx.systemPrompt.section({name:'agent-memory-habit', order:3200})) carrying that same conditional rule inside the stable prefix; the rule is honestly a prompt nudge, not a guarantee, and there is no automatic topical recall — only the index line and the rule enter context, so memory content still requires an explicit memory_recall call; both contributions fail open on any read/parse/registration error (never throws), and the index keeps an idempotent read-only cache keyed strictly by {path, size, mtimeMs}. I4a.1: `inject` is narrowed to ['tools'] and the injection surface is registered conditionally via ctx.inject(['systemPrompt'], scope => scope.systemPrompt.context(...)) — a missing systemPrompt costs only the injection line, never the four tools (the old hard dependency made the whole plugin skip apply()). I3: an ordered bidirectional tag co-occurrence graph built per call from the current store (directed counts kept separate per direction, log(1+lambda*W) compression instead of linear accumulation, per-node outflow normalised to a fixed budget, hub suppression (inDegree/median)^-eta), plus bounded pulse propagation (maxHops/maxStates/maxFieldNeighbors, decay gamma, immediate backflow suppression rho) that adds a capped auxiliary reward graph <= GRAPH_BONUS_CAP to the ranking (final = rel + graph, rel stays the BM25 score that decides match); no module-level mutable state that affects request results (the only one is src/store.ts's tmpSeq, which names atomic-write temp files and never enters recall/scoring/injection), propagation is request-local, and the injection line is untouched. I4a.2: anchor selection now applies an occurrence-rate qualification filter first (a tag on more than ANCHOR_MAX_DF_RATIO = 0.3 of records, configurable via injection.anchorMaxDfRatio, can never become an anchor), then ranks the qualified set by document frequency desc with a code-unit tie-break; fewer than topTags anchors is reported honestly and a corpus whose tags all fail the filter gets an explicit 无可区分锚点 line instead of falling back to the most frequent tag. I2.2: the offline calibration script now draws its negative samples from a frozen, corpus-independent cross-domain vocabulary (scripts/negative-samples.mjs, zero-argument deterministic generator) so the set grows from 12 hand-written queries to 240, and it prints a sensitivity comparison that puts the 12-sample estimate (the old script's own sample) side by side with the full-set estimate, which is what SCALE_A = p50(negatives) and WEAK = p95(negatives) actually rest on. Still print-only: it never writes any file or config, and an empty store exits 0 with a readable hint. I5/修正1: the memory_recall L1 header is a single line whose total length is bounded by HEADER_MAX_CHARS = 448 characters, and that bound holds by construction for ANY query string: the fixed part echoes the scale constants through formatHeaderConstant at a bounded width (an over-wide value is rendered as an approximate value marked with a leading ≈; the exact value stays in the structured scaleA/scaleB/weakThreshold/strongThreshold fields) and the query= echo is bounded by formatHeaderQuery, which truncates the raw query BY CODE POINT FIRST and JSON-escapes only afterwards (so escape sequences are never cut) and marks truncation honestly with …(截断). The old 'single line of <= 400 characters' claim had only ever been measured on three short-query fixtures (388~399): a 200-character query containing quotes/backslashes/newlines measured 742 characters and a 360-character one 932, and a 22-decimal scaleB pushed the fixed part to 413 on its own. It keeps only what is needed to recompute the printed judgement (column order, rel semantics + the two match thresholds, score=disp(final) with both scale constants, limit as the hard display cap, the I2 conclusions novelty/threshold/expanded/kBase->kUsed, the low-confidence cov_max/activation threshold, and the I3 conclusions final=rel+graph / graph bonus cap / graph size / hub-suppressed count / reachable); non-conclusive diagnostics (basisSize/layers/logicalDepth, the explainedRatio+residualRatio conservation, propagation limits/gamma/rho, seed-and-arrival counts, diversity beta) are no longer echoed in the header and remain exact structured fields. The old 1049~1066-character header (measured on this device; evidence: redproof/i5-header-old-measure.txt and i5-header-red.txt) fit only 7~9 rows under RECALL_MAX_CHARS=2000 and echoed the scale constants themselves, so retuning SCALE_A/SCALE_B/WEAK/STRONG used to change how many rows were displayed; test/header.test.mjs now pins that the number of displayed rows (and the truncated flag) is identical across scale configurations. I6.2/I7: the L1 column list is now the single source of truth for four places at once (formatL1's cell-table key order via the exported recallCells, the L1Row field order, the output schema's rows.properties key order, and the actual serialized row key order), all pinned at runtime by test/columns.test.mjs (a schema or cell-table key moved back to the pre-I3 order turns it red), while the printed lines stay byte-identical (verified against the pre-change build over a fixed corpus: 7/7 query/config cases produce identical lines and identical row values, only the header text and the row key order change). The memory_recall description and the L1 header now state the true score formula: final=(rel+graph)×diversity factor, where the factor (1-beta*maxSim, beta=0.3) is applied only when the candidate count is > 5, together with the honest consequence that a diversified score cannot be recomputed from the printed rel/graph alone (beta and maxSim are not printed columns) while match always can be recomputed from the printed rel plus the header thresholds; the header also states the graph/via column semantics, and the old 'no evidence => rel/score are 0.0000' wording is replaced by the precise version (no lexical evidence => rel=0; graph-only arrivals have graph>0 and via=tag:<label>, and their score depends on the scale constants - 0.0000 by default only because SCALE_A 0.0187 exceeds GRAPH_BONUS_CAP 0.018). 修正2: the memory_recall tool description is slimmed from 1182 to 261 characters (<= 300), keeping only the ten-column list (still derived from RECALL_COLUMNS), one rel/match/score sentence, limit as the hard display cap, the never-returns-body rule, and a pointer to docs/recall-contract.md; every detail removed from the description moved verbatim into that document, and test/description.test.mjs pins both layers (the description for length <= 300 plus the five essentials, the document for the moved details) so that the pointer cannot lie. The engine's deferLoading marker IS supported (defineTool option: @deepseek-ai/dsh-tools/lib/index.js:864, type lib/types/schema.d.ts:194-195) but is deliberately NOT adopted: it is a session tool-update mechanism (route ToolUpdate, dsh-llm/lib/types/types.d.ts:365-374; projectToolUpdates dsh-llm/lib/index.js:786-834) and an explicitly deferred baseline tool stays deferred until its first retained tool-addition block (dsh-llm/README.zh.md:162), which for these boot-registered tools would mean the model never sees memory_recall at all. test/graph.test.mjs adds the graph-arrival invariant (returned, rel=0, graph>0, via=tag:, match=none, score === absoluteDisp(rel+graph)).
